name: MS-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 11 points and incumbent Bennie Thompson is running for reelection
Thompson holds a decisive financial edge: about $1.36 million on hand versus roughly $38,000 for Ron Eller
Prediction markets price Thompson near 97% to win, with no outside spending against him
No public polling of the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's 11-point Democratic lean, Thompson's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising advantage over Ron Eller all point the same direction, and markets price this as a near-certain Democratic hold. With no polling or ratings suggesting any competitive threat, the forecast stays at a roughly 21-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Eller within single digits, or a major shift in the national political environment, would be the first sign this race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This western Mississippi district leans Democratic by about 11 points, and incumbent Bennie Thompson is seeking another term with every structural advantage in place. He has raised roughly $928,000 and holds about $1.36 million in cash, while Republican Ron Eller has raised about $64,000 with under $40,000 available. No outside groups are spending against Thompson, and an independent candidate in the field has raised essentially nothing.

No public polls cover the race, and no expert raters list it as competitive. Prediction markets put Thompson's chances near 97%. The forecast therefore expects Thompson to win by roughly 20 points, with uncertainty somewhat elevated because direct polling evidence is absent. The seat is rated Safe Democratic.
